runtime_status: release-candidate; Linux/static/artifact gates pass locally; Windows PowerShell 5.1 provider-sync runtime gate is wired into Windows CI and remains authoritative until exercised there or on the target machine
notes: v7.9.2: Skyrim Forge is merged into this repository at BUNDLED-TOOLS/skyrim-forge and is no longer released separately. The split is what allowed 7.8.0 to ship an installer calling $contract.compatible, a field Forge has never emitted, so a fresh install threw on every run -- two files that had to agree, in two repositories, with no single commit able to test both. TOOLS/Install-SkyrimForge.ps1 copies the in-tree source instead of extracting an archive, preserves Workspaces and the virtualenv across an upgrade (a replace-in-place would have deleted the user's mod work), takes a -ForgeRoot, and proves the install runs with `forge doctor`. Forge 6.0.0 drops the `bundle-contract` command: one repository cannot usefully negotiate a version range with itself, and a stale range can only start rejecting the pack it ships inside. Root CI gained five Forge jobs plus one that installs Forge from this tree end to end -- the job that could not have existed before the merge. 143 canonical skills across 5 provider trees. A real Windows PowerShell 5.1 run then exposed two final-doctor integration bugs: Test-Installed-State.ps1 assigned the read-only $HOME variable via `$home`, and behind that it still called Forge 5.x `bundle-contract`, which Forge 6.0.0 removed. The doctor now uses `$providerHome`, runs `forge doctor`, requires result=PASS/read_only_ready=true, and the parent installer persists child-doctor diagnostics. The skyrim-forge skill and all five provider copies are synchronized to Forge 6.x/versionless SKYRIM_FORGE_ROOT. A second real Windows PowerShell 5.1 run exposed two additional closure defects: a hotfix had written literal \n text into Test-Installed-State.ps1, commenting out the provider-home assignment and causing Join-Path to receive null; and Forge's Hermes registrar still used the interactive `hermes mcp add` path with output hidden, which could wait invisibly for a keypress. The doctor source is now line-safe and regression-checked, while Hermes registration writes through Hermes' config API noninteractively and runs a visible connection test with a 45-second hard bound and five-second progress updates. The release contract also rejects the accidental next-major bundle label anywhere in shipped text or filenames; the bundle release remains 7.9.2. A third real Windows run then reached the final doctor with Forge and all five MCP registrations healthy but reported exactly ten stale bundle skills: release-checklist and skyrim-forge in each provider home. Root-cause reconstruction from the shipped archives showed two independent writers: deterministic ZIP timestamps let the old metadata-based provider copy skip release-checklist when old/new files had identical name/size/time, and the Forge wrapper then replaced the freshly bundled skyrim-forge skill with its separate integration copy. The production provider sync now avoids metadata classification entirely (stage -> SHA-256 verify -> directory swap -> SHA-256 verify), and the AIO marks provider skills bundle-owned so Forge refreshes only INSTALLATION.json plus MCP configuration without rewriting SKILL.md. Forge checked commands also print a start marker and elapsed-time success while suppressing multi-page success JSON.
